title: ADC data comes as two bytes. low is a signed char (as on AVR). What does this print?
explain: low = 0x90 is negative as int8_t. In the OR it is promoted to int and sign-extended to 0xFFFFFF90. The high bits turn all 1. Result 0xFF90 = 65424, not 0x190 = 400. Cast each byte to uint8_t before you combine them.

title: A 74HC00 has 4 NAND gates. You want OR(A, B) using only NAND gates. How many gates do you need?
explain: De Morgan: A OR B = NAND(NOT A, NOT B). A NOT is a NAND with both inputs tied together. So: 2 gates for the two NOTs, 1 gate for the final NAND. That is 3 of your 4 gates. Do not leave the inputs of the 4th gate floating.

title: Next step: UART on the Uno (16 MHz). UBRR = f/16/baud - 1 with integer math, baud 115200. What does this print (UBRR, real baud)?
explain: f/16/baud = 1000000/115200 = 8.68, truncated to 8, minus 1 = 7. The real baud is 16 MHz / (16 * 8) = 125000: 8.5% too fast, so the bytes break. Rounding gives UBRR 8 (111111 baud, 3.5% off). The Arduino core uses double speed (U2X) for a better match.

title: Blink timer, interval 10 ms. loop() runs every 3 ms. How many toggles in 100 ms with last = now?
explain: loop() sees the time only at 0, 3, 6 ... So each toggle comes late (12, 24, 36 ...) and last = now keeps the delay. The delays add up: 8 toggles. With last += interval the average stays at 10 ms and you get 9. Use += for a steady period.

title: STM32 SysTick runs at 16 MHz. You want a 1 ms tick (1 kHz). What is the LOAD value?
explain: SysTick counts from LOAD down to 0. That is LOAD + 1 clocks per period. For 16000 clocks you write 16000 - 1 = 15999. It is the same off-by-one as PSC + 1 and OCR1A - 1.

title: Debounce does nothing, the counter still jumps. Tap the bug.
explain: last = r runs before the compare, so r != last is never true. The timer t never restarts and stable follows every noisy edge. Compare first, then update last at the end of the step.

title: Button on a pin: 4 checks
bullets: A floating input reads random values. Always use a pull-up or pull-down.
INPUT_PULLUP: button between pin and GND. Not pressed = HIGH, pressed = LOW.
External pull-up value: 10 kΩ is common. 1 kΩ wastes 5 mA at 5 V when pressed. Very large values make the edge slow and noisy.
A contact bounces for some ms. Debounce in software (about 50 ms) or with an RC filter, then detect the edge.

pr.title: Less noise: average 128 samples
pr.author: junior-fw
pr.body: The temperature jumps around. Average 128 readings instead of 16.

explain: A 10-bit reading is up to 1023. 128 * 1023 = 130944 does not fit in uint16_t (max 65535). The sum wraps and the average is wrong. 16 samples were safe: 16368. Use a 32-bit sum when you raise the sample count.

title: Pot wiper at 30% of 5 V, 10-bit ADC. The code scales with integers. What does this print?
explain: 30% of 5 V is 1.5 V. 1.5 / 5 * 1023 = 306.9. Integer math cuts the .9, so you get 306. The ADC range is 0..1023, which is 1024 steps. Multiply first (1023 * 30), then divide, or you lose everything.

title: Rust `as` casts on sensor values. What does this print?
explain: `as` between integers keeps the low bits and never panics: 300 as u8 = 300 - 256 = 44. -1i32 as u32 is all ones: 4294967295. A float to int cut the fraction: 3.9 gives 3 (it saturates when out of range). Use u8::try_from(x) when the value must fit.
